title: Supabase authentication fails after Vercel deployment
context: Next.js application using Supabase SSR authentication deployed on Vercel Serverless.
error: HTTP 401 Unauthorized: Auth session missing or cookie invalid during Route Handler execution.
symptoms: Returns 401 in production on server action or API call.

attempts.description: Changed environment variables (regenerated Supabase Anon and Service Role keys)
attempts.reason: The issue was related to authentication cookies not propagating, not invalid API credentials.

attempts.description: Reinstalled dependencies and changed Node.js version from 22 to 20
attempts.reason: Persisted across all Node runtime versions.

attempts.description: Checked middleware matcher configuration and disabled route filters
attempts.reason: Static files loaded middleware but did not fix the session cookie synchronization.

root_cause: Authentication cookie was not correctly propagated. In @supabase/ssr, cookie mutations cannot occur during Server Component rendering; response cookies must be copied back onto request headers inside middleware.ts.

solutions.title: Solution A: Synchronize response cookies back to request headers in middleware
solutions.why_it_works: Ensures cookies mutated or refreshed by Supabase are visible to both Server Actions and downstream Route Handlers without dropping session credentials.
solutions.trade_offs: Slight edge compute latency increase on first request to run getUser().
solutions.limitations: Requires all routes with authenticated actions to pass through middleware matcher.
solutions.author: alexander

solutions.title: Solution B (Alternative approach): Pre-fetch session JWT inside custom Route Handler
solutions.why_it_works: Bypasses browser cookie handling in favor of explicit Bearer token headers.
solutions.trade_offs: Requires manual token refresh logic on the client; not idiomatic for SSR forms.
solutions.limitations: Does not support standard Next.js form actions with cookies.
solutions.author: kenji

author.bio: Full stack engineer working on Next.js + serverless.

discussions.author: dev_kelsey
discussions.content: Can confirm this fixed our team's staging deployment on Vercel! We lost 6 hours debugging key rotations before finding this exact middleware cookie mutation rule.

discussions.author: marcus_io
discussions.content: Be careful to ensure your middleware matcher excludes _next/static or you will run getUser() on every CSS and chunk download.

title: Neon Postgres connection pool exhaustion during Next.js Turbopack dev rebuilds
context: Next.js 15 local dev environment with Prisma connecting to serverless Neon PostgreSQL.
error: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections.
symptoms: Hot module reload opens duplicate connection pools.
Connection pool exhausts after saving 5-6 edits.

attempts.description: Increased max connection limits in database settings
attempts.reason: Turbopack fast reload spawned new processes faster than TCP idle timeouts could reclaim sockets.

root_cause: Next.js dev rebuilds re-evaluate module scopes, instantiating new PrismaClient connections unless attached to the globalThis singleton object.

solutions.title: Solution: Bind Prisma client instance to globalThis singleton
solutions.why_it_works: Prevents creating new TCP connections on hot module reloads.
solutions.limitations: Applicable only to Node runtimes, not Edge workers.
solutions.author: sarah_dev

title: Claude Desktop MCP server hangs on Windows stdio transport over WSL2
context: Configuring Model Context Protocol server inside WSL2 with Windows desktop client.
error: Process spawned without stdout flush; JSON-RPC handshake timed out.
symptoms: Claude Desktop shows agent connecting indefinitely.
No tool declarations returned in UI.
root_cause: Windows wsl.exe stdio stream doesn't autoflush line-delimited JSON-RPC messages without explicit UTF-8 line endings.
